text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- The government faces new criticism of the basic treaty with Romania following a report that the document contains significant changes from the draft version.

- The cabinet decided Friday on a package of measures to tighten tax legislation in 1997. By Sunday, when it met again, the cabinet succeeded in reaching agreement on all issues regarding the 1997 budget, announced spokesman Elemer Kiss.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn opened the 100th Budapest International Exhibition on Friday. (Sat.)
- After the deduction of the increase caused by devaluation, hard currency savings have fallen by HUF 14 billion since the beginning of this year.
- The American development organisation USAID will guarantee $6 million of OTP Bank loans to privately-owned small and medium-sized enterprises, according to a contract signed Friday.
- A consortium led by the international road construction company Betonutepito has won the tender to upgrade a 43-km stretch of the M3 highway.
- The oil exploration company Koolajkutato Rt has won a $10 million tender for the execution of oil rig construction in Syria.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The market of apples, once a valuable asset of Hungary, will collapse this year unless the state provides a HUF1-1.4 billion bailout to farmers, according to Ferenc Inantsy, general secretary of the Apple Product Council. (Sat.)
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Former Polish president Lech Walesa was received by President Arpad Goncz on Saturday in Parliament.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The trade deficit shrank from $2.1 billion to $1.7 billion in January-July 1996 compared to the same period last year, according to the Central Statistics Office.
- Hungarian exporters will have access to the services of the export credit insurer Mehib in branches of Magyar Hitel Bank, according to an agreement signed Friday by the two companies' leaders.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The pharmaceutical firm Richter has applied to the Stock Exchange Council for permission to list nearly 518,000 preferential shares on the market. (Sat.)
- Workers of the Hungarian telecom company Matav bought 2.7 per cent of the firm's HUF 103 billion equity at a discount price last week, decreasing the state's stake to the obligatory 25 per cent.
NEPSZAVA
- Tamas Gyarfas was re-elected as president of the Hungarian Swimming Association on Saturday, two weeks after resigning his post.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327-4040
